text.p: Italian banks and funds have reduced their weight on Italian bonds for the second consecutive month, investing more abroad and on Italian equities, a Reuters Asset Allocation Poll for July showed on Friday.
"The Italian bond market has given us a lot of satisfaction this year and now it's time to look elsewhere for profit," Cariplo's research department said.

Last week's interest rate cut "and other easings on the horizon favour Italian equities more," Cariplo added. The Bank of Italy last Friday reduced the official discount rate to 6.25 percent from 6.75 percent.

"As the market discounts Italy's entry into (Europe's) monetary union from the start, the profit outlook on Italy's bond market diminishes and it becomes a little bit more risky to stay in this sector," an analyst said adding that he is cautious on Italy as a whole. He had reduced his weighting on Italian bonds to 20 percent from 30 previously.

The analyst, who declined to be named, shifted weight from Italian bonds to investments abroad, mostly on foreign equities. Out of a total 40 percent abroad, he placed 10 percent on bonds and 30 percent on equities.

"The economic pickup which started in Britain and the U.S. is now starting to spread throughout Europe and therefore one tries to take advantage of the revaluation of the stock markets which usually precedes the pickup in consumption and investments," the analyst said.

Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI), on the other hand, increased its weight on the Italian bond market because it betted on Italy's interest rates converging towards Germany's. "The convergence process is still not over and we think the Italian bond market will outperform foreign ones," Marcello Esposito, analyst at BCI said.
The Milan based bank favours short term paper, in the region of one to three years.

"We believe in a monetary tightening in Germany in the medium term. This would reduce the profit potential on long BTPs but on short term paper there is still so much room to capture on convergence trades that even with an interest rate hike in Germany, we could see some profit," Esposito added.

Reuters collected the allocation figures from eight Italian banks and investment funds from June 30 and July 2. The data in parenthesis refer to the June survey. The averages in the June survey are based on forecasts from nine analysts one of whom did not participate in this survey. The next survey will be published in September.
Credito Italiano provided the asset allocation only for bonds and is therefore not included in the averages.
